items.problem: Bootstrap inventory omitted MSBuild-linked files outside the source directory.
items.evidence: lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[0] and skill-defects.json items[0]: only four files were mapped although the csproj linked the complete shared shell/resource graph.
items.root_cause: Filesystem recursion cannot see external Include/Link project items.
items.hierarchy_justification: Tier 1 is the highest in-scope reliable fix: the bootstrap can deterministically carry the project graph. A template or prose reminder would still leave agents to discover and reconstruct linked files manually; Tier 0 harness changes are unnecessary.
items.devils_advocate: This is not redundant with physical recursion because the omitted files live outside Source. If the agent ignores prose, the script still copies and maps them. A rerun can directly count the required linked outputs.
items.change: Extend Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 to resolve common MSBuild path properties and copy explicit linked source/resource items to their Link paths before rewrite and triage.
items.expected_effect: Shared shells, pages, dictionaries, code, and assets are copied and represented in MIGRATION-MAPPING.md without manual reconstruction.
items.falsifiable_check: Running the bootstrap on TouchKeyboardTextInput copies App.xaml, MainPage.xaml, both scenario XAML files, Styles\Styles.xaml, shared code, and linked assets; required missing count is 0 and legacy Windows.UI.Xaml residue outside .uwp-source is 0.

items.problem: The 0xc000027b startup hint misclassified an opaque Microsoft.UI.Xaml failure and lacked a safe no-stack diagnostic path.
items.evidence: migration-score.json features[0..1] and lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[1]: both features were unreachable after repeated speculative edits driven by the unsupported-projection hint.
items.root_cause: The native code is a broad symptom class, not proof of an unsupported startup API.
items.hierarchy_justification: The first diagnostic is emitted by Tier 1 launch tooling, so correcting it there is harder to miss than prose alone. Detailed XAML bisection remains Tier 3 because a generic script cannot safely infer which application resource or control is invalid.
items.devils_advocate: The existing helper detected the crash but supplied the wrong likely cause; this changes the actionable signal rather than duplicating detection. If the detailed prose is ignored, the corrected helper still directs the first investigation toward XAML/resources.
items.change: Correct Test-AppLaunch.ps1's executable hint and add resource-preserving XAML isolation guidance to the existing startup-crashes pattern.
items.expected_effect: Agents inspect startup XAML/resource integrity before deleting dictionaries or deferring features when no managed stack exists.
items.falsifiable_check: A rerun that captures 0xc000027b in Microsoft.UI.Xaml.dll prints the XAML/resource-first hint, retains custom resource providers during isolation, and either identifies the failing XAML region or reaches a running window.

items.problem: The skill prescribed the unsupported winapp build command.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 15 rejected the command; turn 16 dotnet build succeeded.
items.root_cause: Compilation and packaged launch responsibilities were conflated.
items.hierarchy_justification: This is command selection, so no new Tier 1 wrapper or Tier 2 scaffold is warranted; the plugin explicitly uses native dotnet commands. Correcting the invoked command at its instruction sites is the smallest reliable change.
items.devils_advocate: dotnet build was already mentioned elsewhere, but the prominent Step 3 command contradicted it and the agent followed the wrong command. The observable rerun signal is the complete absence of winapp build.
items.change: Replace winapp build instructions with dotnet build and clarify that Test-AppLaunch.ps1 owns packaged launch.
items.expected_effect: The first compile command works across supported environments without a wasted retry.
items.falsifiable_check: On rerun, no winapp build invocation occurs and the initial dotnet build reaches a normal MSBuild success or actionable compiler error.
